title: Reliability and Resilience
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of reliability and resilience in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply reliability and resilience to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Reliability and Resilience is lesson 184 in Security, Reliability, and Production Practices. Production code must treat inputs and dependencies as untrusted, make failure behavior explicit, protect sensitive information, and provide repeatable verification and release steps.
content.why_it_matters: Production quality includes safe failure behavior, observable operation, and a repeatable way to ship updates. This lesson focuses on reliability and resilience and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production code must treat inputs and dependencies as untrusted, make failure behavior explicit, protect sensitive information, and provide repeatable verification and release steps.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for reliability and resilience. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Defensive programming
items.text: For defensive programming, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to reliability and resilience, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Timeouts and cancellation
items.text: Await I/O-bound tasks, pass cancellation tokens across boundaries, and protect shared mutable state explicitly.

items.title: Retry policies and backoff
items.text: Production behavior must fail safely and be observable. Validate untrusted input, enforce authorization at the server boundary, protect secrets, retry only appropriate transient failures, and verify the released artifact.

items.title: Idempotent operations
items.text: For idempotent operations, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to reliability and resilience, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Graceful failure
items.text: For graceful failure, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to reliability and resilience, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Resource limits and recovery
items.text: Use explicit paths and scoped resource disposal; test missing files, permission failures, and partial data.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates reliability and resilience. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates reliability and resilience rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for reliability and resilience before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
